english_translation: Potatoes are being sold at the market, where a woman wearing a light-coloured apron stands beside a man in a red shirt and a sky-blue jacket.

dialogue.shona: Pamusika parikutengeswa mbatatisi. Mudzimai wakamira akapfeka hapuroni yakati chenerukire nemurume wakapfeka hembe tsvuku nebhachi rine ruvara rwedenga risina makore.
dialogue.english: Potatoes are on sale at the market, where a woman in a light apron stands with a man wearing a red shirt and a clear sky-blue jacket.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Pamusika [on / at musika] • parikutengeswa [on / at rikutengeswa] • mbatatisi [mbatatisi] • Mudzimai [in / singular dzimai] • wakamira [you/he (past) mira] • akapfeka [he/she (past) pfeka] • hapuroni [hapuroni] • yakati [it (past) ti]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('wakamira')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'wakamira' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Colours & Describing Objects in Shona ('tsvuku')
grammar_notes.content: This passage uses colour vocabulary such as 'tsvuku'. Shona has three traditional core colour adjectives that change their prefix slightly to match the noun they describe: '-chena' (white/clean, e.g., 'ruvara ruchena' or 'shangu chena'), '-tema / nhema' (black/dark, e.g., 'mota nhema' or 'ruvara rutema'), and '-tsvuku' (red/bright brown, e.g., 'mota tsvuku' or 'ruvara rutsvuku'). For other colours like green ('girinhi'), blue ('bhuruu'), or orange ('orenji'), speakers typically say 'ruvara rwe-' ('the colour of...') followed by the colour name, as in 'ruvara rwegirinhi' (green).
grammar_notes.rule: Core Colours: -chena (white), -tema / nhema (black), -tsvuku (red) | Phrase pattern: ruvara rwe-[colour] (e.g., ruvara rwegirinhi)

grammar_notes.title: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('Pamusika')
grammar_notes.content:
Look at how location is expressed with 'Pamusika'. Instead of separate prepositions like 'on', 'to', or 'in', Shona attaches one of three location prefixes directly to the front of a noun:
• 'pa-' means 'at' or 'on' a specific point or surface (e.g., 'patafura' = on the table, 'pamusika' = at the market, 'pasi' = on the ground).
• 'ku-' means 'to', 'from', or 'at' a general destination (e.g., 'kuchikoro' = to school, 'kumusha' = to the rural home, 'kubasa' = at/to work).
• 'mu-' means 'inside' an enclosed space (e.g., 'mumba' = inside the house, 'muguta' = in the city, 'mumugwagwa' = in the road).
grammar_notes.rule: pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)

cultural_notes.title: Nyanga Seed Potatoes & Market Trading ('Mbatatisi Pamusika')
cultural_notes.content: Zimbabwe's cool, frost-free high altitudes in Nyanga are the country's premier region for growing potatoes ('mbatatisi'), which are sold in 15kg pockets and small heaps at urban and peri-urban markets.

active_exercises.prompt: Complete this sentence about tree leaves: 'Mashizha emuti uyu ane ruvara ______.' (The leaves of this tree have a green colour.)
active_exercises.explanation: 'Ruvara rwegirinhi' expresses 'green colour' when describing fresh leaves ('mashizha').

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Mukoma wangu akatenga mota chena nezuro.'
options: My older brother bought a white car yesterday.
My sister is wearing a red dress today.
Which bus goes to the city centre?
The black truck is parked beside the road.
active_exercises.correct_answer: My older brother bought a white car yesterday.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Mukoma wangu' = 'My older brother', 'akatenga' = 'bought', 'mota chena' = 'a white car', 'nezuro' = 'yesterday'.

active_exercises.prompt: If a farmer says 'Gore rino takawana goho guru pamunda pedu', what happened?
options: They are waiting for the rain to start next month
They obtained a big harvest from their field this year
The river flooded and washed away the bridge
A strong wind blew from the east all afternoon
active_exercises.correct_answer: They obtained a big harvest from their field this year
active_exercises.explanation: 'Takawana' = 'we obtained/got', 'goho guru' = 'a big harvest', 'pamunda pedu' = 'from our field'.
